statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(words) such that words[i] is a prefix of s. A byte array w is a prefix of s iff len(w) <= len(s) and for every j with 0 <= j < len(w), w[j] = s[j]. Equivalently, r = #{ i | 0 <= i < len(words) and len(words[i]) <= len(s) and (for every j with 0 <= j < len(words[i]), words[i][j] = s[j]) }. Each index is counted separately, so duplicate strings in words are counted once per occurrence.
preconditions: words is a slice with 1 <= len(words) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 10; 1 <= len(s) <= 10; every byte of every words[i] and of s is an ASCII lowercase letter (97 <= byte <= 122).
